name: Veegaland Developers Ltd
title: Veegaland Developers Ltd - 544923 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Kerala residential developer posts Q2 revenue up 28.7% to INR106.3 cr and PAT up 92%, but the read is mostly demand and margin mix; no supply-side capacity signal, and ~INR500 cr of unrecognised revenue plus ~INR1,080 cr order book gives visibility.

summary.headline: Veegaland Q2 FY27 revenue rose 28.7% YoY to INR106.34 crore and PAT rose 92% to INR15.99 crore, with PAT margin at 14.7%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR106.34 crore, up 28.66% YoY, with EBITDA (incl. other income) of INR22.78 crore (up 77%) and EBITDA margin of 20.90%, up 550 bps. PAT was INR15.99 crore, up 92%, at a 14.70% margin. H1 FY27 revenue was INR180.66 crore (up 45%) and PAT was INR25.71 crore (up 123%). Management attributed margin gains to luxe-series mix, cost efficiencies on near-complete projects, and treasury income on RERA-linked fixed deposits. The company listed on 18 September 2026 after a INR210 crore IPO.

segments.name: Premium / mid-premium
segments.commentary: Higher-volume, lower-ticket segment; management says demand is strong across segments. Average selling price rose from INR8,539 per sq ft in June to INR9,286 in September, per the call.

segments.name: Luxe series
segments.commentary: High-margin, low-volume; two luxe projects, with Fortune launched and already in ongoing status. Luxe launches in H2 FY26 are now flowing through revenue and lifting margins.

guidance_outlook: Management does not give pre-sales or GDV projections; it expects strong momentum but declined to quantify it.
Three upcoming projects with estimated GDV of about INR450 crore (Sarovar, East Port, and Fortune, which has since launched) are slated for launch in Q3 FY27 or early Q4 FY27.
Land-bank launches expected 6 to 9 months out; management declined to give GDV for them.
Margins expected to hold steady on an unchanged product mix, though material prices are being monitored.
Leverage is not to exceed about 0.5:1 in the mid-term; no significant increase in debt is planned.
Proceeds of the IPO are earmarked for ongoing projects, planned acquisitions and general corporate purposes.
capex_capacity: Land bank is about 6.4 acres, mostly in Kochi with some in Kozhikode; the company holds no Trivandrum land after launching Lluvia Gardens (163 units).
Portfolio is 12 ongoing and 3 upcoming projects: 2 in Thrissur, 2 in Kozhikode, 3 in Trivandrum and the rest in Kochi.
Projects are boutique apartment schemes of about 75 to 150 units; preferred land parcels are around 1 to 1.25 acres for faster turnaround.
Management is scouting new land to support a FY29 plan and is considering new geographies in neighbouring areas; no specific location announced.
Unencumbered cash is about INR180 crore, with further funds in RERA escrow accounts.
demand_pricing: Pre-sales value rose 37.6% YoY and area booked rose 19.6% YoY; gross collections rose 88.2% YoY.
Q2 pre-sales were about INR174 crore.
Amora (Kochi) was 68% booked within about 4 months of launch.
NRI buyers account for about 48% to 50% of sales, and Middle East-based Malayalis are buying a second home in Kerala.
Q1 FY27 pre-sales were unusually high, which management attributes to Middle East conflict-driven demand.
Cancellations after agreement execution are very low; management says cancelled units were resold at higher prices.
Management says its prices are below listed national peers such as Sobha and Prestige for comparable offerings.

qa_highlights.question: Are there plans for projects outside Kerala?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is evaluating neighbouring geographies but has named none yet; it will announce once plans are finalised.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook, and can margins return to the FY23 level of about 21-23%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are sustainable on a stable product mix, citing luxe-series mix and cost efficiencies; it gave no project-level margins or FY23 comparison.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR1,080 crore order book is still unrecognised, and over what period?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR500 crore is unrecognised and should be recognised up to FY30-31, not linearly, with larger chunks in FY27 and FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Is incremental borrowing needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said balance-sheet borrowing is not needed but project term loans will be taken; leverage will stay below about 0.5:1 in the mid-term.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current cancellation rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no figure; it said post-agreement cancellations are very few because buyers are almost all end-users.

qa_highlights.question: How will sales hold up given rate hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said premium and luxe buyers are less rate-sensitive and that NRI buyers often pay without bank loans; it cited a 25 bps hike.

risks_watch: Revenue visibility rests on about INR500 crore of unrecognised order value, and pre-sales strength in Q1 FY27 was flagged as partly event-driven (Middle East).
NRI demand (48% to 50% of sales) is exposed to Gulf geopolitics.
Material cost inputs (steel, cables, PVC, sanitary) are being watched; management says there is no margin squeeze yet.
Treasury income on RERA-linked deposits is a meaningful part of EBITDA and PAT.
Watch the Q3 FY27 launches (Sarovar, East Port) and their sales pace against the INR450 crore GDV estimate.
Land acquisition pace and new geography decisions; land bank is only about 6.4 acres.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, pricing and margins, but evasive on forward numbers: management declined to give pre-sales, GDV, cancellation rate and land-bank carrying value, and gave no FY23 margin comparison.
key_quotes: Our pre-sales grew by 37.6% year-on-year in value terms, while the area booked increased by 19.6%.
So, on a margin,on a forward-looking basis, we are confident that we'll be able to maintain constant, stable margins in the market.
But at the same time, there is an increase in selling price because of the market and market demand.
we do not have a risk of non-payment because the title of the project or the product is not transferred until every rupee is paid by him or her.

growth.why: No numeric revenue guidance; management declined to quantify pre-sales momentum, but ~INR450 crore GDV of three projects is slated for launch in Q3 FY27 or early Q4 FY27 and the INR1,080 crore order book (about INR500 crore unrecognised) plus pre-sales up 37.6% YoY support a moderate growth outlook.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin rose 550 bps to 20.90% and gross margin to 30.9% (from 26%) on luxe mix and cost efficiencies, but management gave no FY23 21-23% comparison and flagged material cost watch, with treasury income a meaningful part of PAT.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Three upcoming projects with ~INR450 crore GDV (Sarovar, East Port, Fortune) slated for launch in Q3 FY27 or early Q4 FY27, plus land-bank launches 6-9 months out, though no physical capacity figures are given for a boutique developer.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Pre-sales up 37.6% YoY and area booked up 19.6% YoY, with Q2 pre-sales about INR174 crore and INR1,080 crore order book (about INR500 crore unrecognised) backing volume, though Q1 was partly event-driven (Middle East).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Land bank is only about 6.4 acres with no Trivandrum land left, and management is scouting land for an FY29 plan and neighbouring geographies, but no specific location or capex amount announced.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no numeric revenue or margin guidance and declined to quantify pre-sales momentum, so there is no formal guidance to raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1 pre-sales were flagged as event-driven (Middle East), NRI buyers are 48-50% of sales and exposed to Gulf geopolitics, and material costs (steel, cables, PVC) are being monitored.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: Q3 FY27 to early Q4 FY27
rows.why: Sarovar and East Port (with Fortune already launched) slated for launch with ~INR450 crore combined GDV, and boutique schemes of 75-150 units are the standard format.

rows.label: Unrecognised order book converts to revenue
rows.why: About INR500 crore of the INR1,080 crore order book is unrecognised, with larger chunks expected in FY27 and FY28 (recognised up to FY30-31), supporting revenue visibility.

rows.label: Leverage capped near 0.5:1
rows.why: Debt-equity is 0.15% today and management says leverage will not exceed about 0.5:1 mid-term, with no significant new balance-sheet borrowing planned beyond project term loans.

rows.label: Expansion into neighbouring geographies
rows.why: Management is evaluating neighbouring geographies to support an FY29 plan but has named none, and will announce only once plans are finalised.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, pricing (ASP up from INR8,539 to INR9,286 per sq ft) and margin sustainability, but evasive on forward numbers such as pre-sales, GDV, cancellation rate and FY23 margin comparison; analysts pressed on margin durability, order-book timing and rate sensitivity.
